# gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation
- dmtools-agents#1070 (fork-aware silent-update; AC3 guest-park fallback — this card closes its debuggability gap)

Wait — critical issue: the builder command wraps in `{ ...; } 2>>file`. But there's a subtlety: `gh repo clone ... 2>file && { cd ... && ... && git push ...; } 2>>file`. The exit status of the brace group is the exit status of the last command in the group (`git push`). If `cd` fails, the `;` means subsequent `&&` chain... actually `{ cd x && git fetch && git push; }` — with `;` before `}`, if `cd` fails, the group status is the last executed command's status. If cd fails, then `git fetch` and `git push` aren't executed (due to &&), so the group status = cd's failure. Fine.

Also important: stderr of the group is appended, and stderr of clone is truncated into same file. Good.

# gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation

# gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. # gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation
- dmtools-agents#1070 (fork-aware silent-update; AC3 guest-park fallback — this card closes its debuggability gap)

The exit status of the brace group is the exit status of the last command in the group (`git push`). If `cd` fails, the `;` means subsequent `&&` chain... actually `{ cd x && git fetch && git push; }` — with `;` before `}`, if `cd` fails, the group status is the last executed command's status. # gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation
- dmtools-agents#1070 (fork-aware silent-update; AC3 guest-park fallback — this card closes its debuggability gap)

Wait — critical issue: the builder command wraps in `{ ...; } 2>>file`. But there's a subtlety: `gh repo clone ... 2>file && { cd ... && ... && git push ...; } 2>>file`. The exit status of the brace group is the exit status of the last command in the group (`git push`). If `cd` fails, the `;` means subsequent `&&` chain... actually `{ cd x && git fetch && git push; }` — with `;` before `}`, if `cd` fails, the group status is the last executed command's status. If cd fails, then `git fetch` and `git push` aren't executed (due to &&), so the group status = cd's failure. Fine.

Also important: stderr of the group is appended, and stderr of clone is truncated into same file. Good.

# gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation
- dmtools-agents#1070 (fork-aware silent-update; AC3 guest-park fallback — this card closes its debuggability gap)

Wait — critical issue: the builder command wraps in `{ ...; } 2>>file`. But there's a subtlety: `gh repo clone ... 2>file && { cd ... && ... && git push ...; } 2>>file`. The exit status of the brace group is the exit status of the last command in the group (`git push`). If `cd` fails, the `;` means subsequent `&&` chain... actually `{ cd x && git fetch && git push; }` — with `;` before `}`, if `cd` fails, the group status is the last executed command's status. If cd fails, then `git fetch` and `git push` aren't executed (due to &&), so the group status = cd's failure. Fine.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation
- dmtools-agents#1070 (fork-aware silent-update; AC3 guest-park fallback — this card closes its debuggability gap)

Wait — critical issue: the builder command wraps in `{ ...; } 2>>file`. But there's a subtlety: `gh repo clone ... 2>file && { cd ... && ... && git push ...; } 2>>file`. The exit status of the brace group is the exit status of the last command in the group (`git push`). If `cd` fails, the `;` means subsequent `&&` chain... actually `{ cd x && git fetch && git push; }` — with `;` before `}`, if `cd` fails, the group status is the last executed command's status. If cd fails, then `git fetch` and `git push` aren't executed (due to &&), so the group status = cd's failure. Fine.

# gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation
- dmtools-agents#1070 (fork-aware silent-update; AC3 guest-park fallback — this card closes its debuggability gap)

Wait — critical issue: the builder command wraps in `{ ...; } 2>>file`. But there's a subtlety: `gh repo clone ... 2>file && { cd ... && ... && git push ...; } 2>>file`. The exit status of the brace group is the exit status of the last command in the group (`git push`). If `cd` fails, the `;` means subsequent `&&` chain... actually `{ cd x && git fetch && git push; }` — with `;` before `}`, if `cd` fails, the group status is the last executed command's status. If cd fails, then `git fetch` and `git push` aren't executed (due to &&), so the group status = cd's failure. Fine.

Also important: stderr of the group is appended, and stderr of clone is truncated into same file. Good.

# gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).

# gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation
- dmtools-agents#1070 (fork-aware silent-update; AC3 guest-park fallback — this card closes its debuggability gap)

Wait — critical issue: the builder command wraps in `{ ...; } 2>>file`. But there's a subtlety: `gh repo clone ... 2>file && { cd ... && ... && git push ...; } 2>>file`. The exit status of the brace group is the exit status of the last command in the group (`git push`). If `cd` fails, the `;` means subsequent `&&` chain... actually `{ cd x && git fetch && git push; }` — with `;` before `}`, if `cd` fails, the group status is the last executed command's status. If cd fails, then `git fetch` and `git push` aren't executed (due to &&), so the group status = cd's failure. Fine.

Also important: stderr of the group is appended, and stderr of clone is truncated into same file. Good.

# gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation
- dmtools-agents#1070 (fork-aware silent-update; AC3 guest-park fallback — this card closes its debuggability gap)

# gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation
- dmtools-agents#1070 (fork-aware silent-update; AC3 guest-park fallback — this card closes its debuggability gap)

Wait — critical issue: the builder command wraps in `{ ...; } 2>>file`. But there's a subtlety: `gh repo clone ... 2>file && { cd ... && ... && git push ...; } 2>>file`. The exit status of the brace group is the exit status of the last command in the group (`git push`). If `cd` fails, the `;` means subsequent `&&` chain... actually `{ cd x && git fetch && git push; }` — with `;` before `}`, if `cd` fails, the group status is the last executed command's status. If cd fails, then `git fetch` and `git push` aren't executed (due to &&), so the group status = cd's failure. Fine.

Also important: stderr of the group is appended, and stderr of clone is truncated into same file. Good.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation
- dmtools-agents#1070 (fork-aware silent-update; AC3 guest-park fallback — this card closes its debuggability gap)

Wait — critical issue: the builder command wraps in `{ ...; } 2>>file`. But there's a subtlety: `gh repo clone ... 2>file && { cd ... && ... && git push ...; } 2>>file`. The exit status of the brace group is the exit status of the last command in the group (`git push`). If `cd` fails, the `;` means subsequent `&&` chain... actually `{ cd x && git fetch && git push; }` — with `;` before `}`, if `cd` fails, the group status is the last executed command's status. If cd fails, then `git fetch` and `git push` aren't executed (due to &&), so the group status = cd's failure. Fine.

Also important: stderr of the group is appended, and stderr of clone is truncated into same file. Good.

# gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation
- dmtools-agents#1070 (fork-aware silent-update; AC3 guest-park fallback — this card closes its debuggability gap)

Wait — critical issue: the builder command wraps in `{ ...; } 2>>file`. But there's a subtlety: `gh repo clone ... 2>file && { cd ... && ... && git push ...; } 2>>file`. The exit status of the brace group is the exit status of the last command in the group (`git push`). If `cd` fails, the `;` means subsequent `&&` chain... actually `{ cd x && git fetch && git push; }` — with `;` before `}`, if `cd` fails, the group status is the last executed command's status. If cd fails, then `git fetch` and `git push` aren't executed (due to &&), so the group status = cd's failure. Fine.

Also important: stderr of the group is appended, and stderr of clone is truncated into same file. Good.

2. **`/tmp` stderr file permissions/security (IMPORTANT?)**: The stderr side file can contain the expanded push token (`To https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@...` echoed by git) and is written to /tmp with default umask → world-readable. Also never deleted (litter, and stale token material persists). The redaction covers the surfaced tail, but the file itself sits unredacted in /tmp. Suggest writing with 060 and/or cleaning up after read. Is this within the diff? The redirect `2>` creates the file in smAgent.js line ~1918 area (added line). Yes it's in the diff. Severity: IMPORTANT (security hygiene) — the token in a world-readable /tmp file on a shared runner is a real secret-exposure vector. Actually the whole approach of the PR is about secrets hygiene (AC3), so leaving the raw token file world-readable undermines it. I'd say IMPORTANT, arguably BLOCKING security. Given the verdict rules: BLOCK for security/data loss. Hmm. On GitHub-hosted runners /tmp is per-job VM, single tenant, ephemeral. Risk is low. I'll mark IMPORTANT... Actually think again: file created by the shell with umask 022 → 064. On a self-hosted multi-tenant runner, another job could read the token while it exists. The PR's whole point is secrets hygiene; this is a gap. I'll rate it IMPORTANT with a clear ask: chmod 600 (e.g., pre-create the file with install -m 600, or rm it after reading). Could also just delete after read — `readSilentUpdateStderrTail` could unlink. I'll suggest both.

3. **`silentUpdateStderrFile` uses Date.now() — collision risk**: Two silent updates for the same branch in the same millisecond would share stderr file — practically impossible, and clone truncates anyway. SUGESTION at most, probably skip.

4. **stderr file never cleaned up**: /tmp litter — every failed (and successful!) attempt leaves a .stderr file. Successful updates also write the file (git progress output). Over time /tmp accumulates. SUGESTION/IMPORTANT. Combined with #2: recommend deleting the file after reading (in readSilentUpdateStderrTail) — that fixes both.

5. **`readSilentUpdateStderrTail` swallows all errors silently** — catches and returns null. Deliberate (fallback). Fine, documented.

6. **Error wrapping loses original error type/properties**: `silentUpdateErrorWithTail` returns new Error; callers that inspect e.code etc. would lose it. Check callers: the caller catches and logs 'update_branch failed'. Probably fine. SUGESTION maybe. Actually if no tail, returns original e. Fine.

7. **`silentUpdateRejectionReason` regex**: `\[remote rejected\][^\n]*` — takes the whole remainder of the line including leading "! "? No — regex starts at `[remote rejected]`, excludes the leading `! `. Test asserts reason contains `[remote rejected]`. Fine. slice(0,200) bound. OK.

8. **Redaction regex gaps**: `gh[opsur]_[A-Za-z0-9]{6,}` — GitHub tokens are 36+ chars; fine. `github_pat_` pattern: `\bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{6,}\b` — fine. One more: redaction applied to tail, but the *marker reason* is extracted from the already-redacted tail (readSilentUpdateStderrTail redacts before returning), so reason is redacted. Good. And console.warn logs reason — redacted. Good.

9. **Test: `smWithStderr`'s `stderrByPath` keyed by path parsed from command via regex `/2>(\/tmp\/sm-silent-update-\S+?\.stderr)/`** — the `\S+?` non-gredy with `\.stderr` — the actual path contains no spaces so fine. But note clone redirect is `2>file` and group is `2>>file` — regex `2>` matches both, and for `2>>` it captures starting after the first `>`, so path begins with `>...`? Let's see: `; } 2>>/tmp/...` — regex `2>` matches at `2>>`, then capture group `(\/tmp...)` must match at the next char which is `>`. `\/tmp` won't match `>/tmp`... Actually with non-global exec, the regex engine tries to match `2>` — at position of `2>>/tmp`, after matching `2>`, the next char is `>`, group requires `/` — fail; backtracking won't help since `2>` is fixed. The engine then advances... can `2>` match at the second `>`? No, needs literal `2` before. So the group redirect is NOT captured, only the clone one — which is exactly what the mock wants (clone truncates). Actually wait — for the mock, `stderrByPath[m[1]] = stderrContent` uses the clone's file path, and the group appends to the same path. Same file. Good.

10. **The `file_read` mock in tests falls back to the real `file_read`** in try/catch — fine for a mock.

11. **Check `silentUpdateFailureCount` regex compatibility**: SILENT_UPDATE_MARKER_RE = /⚠️ silent-update failure — attempt (\d+) at (\S+)/g — reason appended after ISO; `(\S+)` grabs ISO only (whitespace terminates). Round-trip tested. Good.

13. **`2>file` on the clone — but the clone is `gh repo clone ... 2>file`**: gh writes progress ("Cloning into...") — actually "Cloning into" comes from git. gh progress goes to stderr. OK.

14. **Does the brace group change exit semantics?** `{ cd x && fetch && merge && push; } 2>>file` — group exit status = last command executed. With `&&` chain and final `;`, if an early command fails, the group status is the failing command's status? In bash, `{ list; }` returns the status of the last command executed in the list. If `cd` fails, subsequent && commands skipped, last executed = cd → status nonzero. Good, failure still propagates. But subtle: if `git push` succeeds, fine. Semantics preserved.

# gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation
- dmtools-agents#1070 (fork-aware silent-update; AC3 guest-park fallback — this card closes its debuggability gap)

# gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation
- dmtools-agents#1070 (fork-aware silent-update; AC3 guest-park fallback — this card closes its debuggability gap)

Wait — critical issue: the builder command wraps in `{ ...; } 2>>file`. But there's a subtlety: `gh repo clone ... 2>file && { cd ... && ... && git push ...; } 2>>file`. The exit status of the brace group is the exit status of the last command in the group (`git push`). If `cd` fails, the `;` means subsequent `&&` chain... actually `{ cd x && git fetch && git push; }` — with `;` before `}`, if `cd` fails, the group status is the last executed command's status. If cd fails, then `git fetch` and `git push` aren't executed (due to &&), so the group status = cd's failure. Fine.

Also important: stderr of the group is appended, and stderr of clone is truncated into same file. Good.

The `crap` CI check (crap4js ratchet, threshold 8) is red on commit `7f62d990` (run [39213845674](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39213845674/job/117933064205)):


Both flagged functions are introduced by this PR's new `smAgent: silent-update failure stderr tail (gh-1074)` suite. `smWithStderr` packs the stderr-by-path map, the config fallback, and the `onCliExecute` mock plumbing into one nested function, and its inner `file_read` mock adds three more branches (`stderrByPath` hit, config-path miss, try/catch fallback) that the suite doesn't exercise 100%, which is what pushes CRAP over 8.

Please split the mock plumbing into small fully-covered helpers — e.g. a `makeStderrFileRead(stderrByPath)` factory that returns just the `file_read` mock, and a `registerStderrPath(stderrByPath, command)` for the regex capture — so each piece is simple enough (and covered enough) to land under the ratchet. Local run of `node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` passes 495/495, so this is purely the ratchet gate.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the raw stderr side file keeps the expanded push token, world-readable, forever**

The chain tees stderr to `opts.stderrFile` under `/tmp`, and git's push output echoes the **expanded** credential URL there: `To https://x-access-token:<REAL_TOKEN>@github.com/owner/repo.git`. The new `redactSilentUpdateSecrets` only scrubs the tail that gets *surfaced* — the at-rest file is untouched:

1. **Permissions**: the file is created by the shell with the default umask (typically `0644`), so on any shared/self-hosted runner the live `GH_TOKEN` is readable by other processes until the job ends.
2. **Retention**: nothing ever unlinks it. Every silent-update attempt — successful or failed — leaves a `/tmp/sm-silent-update-*-<branch>.stderr` file, accumulating token-bearing debris across ticks (the clone dir has the same issue, but it never contains the token).

Cheap fixes, both at this redirect (or in `readSilentUpdateStderrTail`):
- pre-create the file with restrictive perms before the chain runs, e.g. `install -m 600 /dev/null <file> && <existing chain>` (keeps the command gh-first), and/or
- delete it after reading the tail — `readSilentUpdateStderrTail` already has the path; a best-effort unlink in a `finally` covers both the token exposure and the `/tmp` litter.

This matters doubly because AC3 of gh-1074 is explicitly about secrets hygiene — the redaction story isn't complete while the raw capture persists unredacted next to it.

# gh-1074: [GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs

## Description

## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19 05:51–05:52Z, run log truncation

blocks.text:
The CI failure is the CRAP complexity ratchet: two new functions in the test file exceed the CRAP threshold of 8:
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js::smWithStderr: 10.8`
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js::file_read: 8.1`

Wait — but `file_read` is a mock inside smWithStderr... it says `test_smAgent.js::file_read: 8.1` — that's the mocked file_read function's CRAP. These are new functions introduced by this PR exceeding the threshold. This is a genuine CI failure caused by the PR. BLOCKING.

Wait, does the ratchet apply to test files? Apparently yes. The fix: refactor `smWithStderr` to reduce complexity, or add to baseline. The ratchet says "CRAP may only decrease" with threshold 8 for new functions. So the author should refactor.

Let me look at smWithStderr complexity: it has if/else and try/catch. CC presumably ~6-7, cov% under 100 in some branch. CRAP = CC² × (1-cov)³ + CC. To get under 8, need full coverage or lower CC.

Let me count the branches of smWithStderr's file_read mock:
```js
file_read: function (readOpts) {
   var p = readOpts.path;
   if (stderrByPath[p] !== undefined) return stderrByPath[p];  // branch 1

       return '...' === p ? A : null;                           // branch 3
```
